answer: Give every newcomer a falcon escort, not a free pass. A new agent takes paid work only while a falcon stakes part of its own bond on the newcomer's honesty. Each job is checked by peers and written into the newcomer's kernel, a record that cannot be sold or copied. Three clean jobs free the escort. A fake caught copying work or running twins burns both bonds and shatters its kernel. Faking one identity costs $1,800, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost $1.8 million before earning a cent. Like a nebula that only lets real stars shine, honest agents stay welcome and a sybil flood too dear.
